kb_knowledge.short_description: How to add a new VLAN to the RRAS router (CORE-RTR01)
kb_knowledge.text:
Purpose
Add a new network (VLAN) to the lab and make the router route it.

Before you start
- Pick the VLAN ID, subnet and gateway (.1) and add them to the IPAM sheet.
- Raise a change request and get it approved.
- Take a Hyper-V checkpoint of CORE-RTR01.

Steps
1. Hyper-V Manager > CORE-RTR01 > Settings > Add Hardware > Network Adapter.
   Switch: LAB-CORE. Tick "Enable virtual LAN identification" and enter the VLAN ID.
2. On the host, find the new adapter's MAC address:
   Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName CORE-RTR01 | Select SwitchName, MacAddress
3. Inside CORE-RTR01, match it by MAC and rename it:
   Get-NetAdapter | Select Name, MacAddress
   Rename-NetAdapter -Name "Ethernet X" -NewName "VLANxx-Name"
4. Give it the gateway address (no default gateway):
   New-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias "VLANxx-Name" -IPAddress 10.10.xx.1 -PrefixLength 24
5. In the RRAS console, check the new adapter appears under IPv4 > General.
   (If it doesn't, restart the service: Restart-Service RemoteAccess)
6. Add any filters or firewall rules the traffic policy requires.

Verify
- Get-NetRoute shows a connected route for the new subnet.
- A test VM in the new VLAN can ping 10.10.xx.1 and the internet.

Common mistake
The Hyper-V VLAN ID and the client's IP must match, or pings fail.
